traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests clearly exist for this story and are passing.
1) Core rule implementation - File: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Exports an ESLint rule whose meta.docs.description is: "Validate format and syntax of @story, @req, and @implements annotations" which matches the story’s core goal. - The rule is annotated with this story and its requirements: /** * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * ... * @req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION - Ensure rule create function validates annotations syntax * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Implement formatting checks per specification * @req REQ-PATH-FORMAT - Validate @story paths follow expected patterns (in Program and validateStoryAnnotation JSDoc) * @req REQ-REQ-FORMAT - Validate @req identifiers follow expected patterns (in Program and validateReqAnnotation JSDoc) * @req REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT - Handle annotations split across multiple lines (in processComment/processCommentLine JSDoc) * @req REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING - Support reasonable variations in whitespace and formatting (in processComment JSDoc) * @req REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY - Provide specific error messages for different format violations (in validateStoryAnnotation/validateReqAnnotation JSDoc) */ - validateStoryAnnotation(...) implements REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION and REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY by: - trimming and collapsing whitespace in the raw value - checking empty values and reporting invalidStoryFormat with details from buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", ...) - applying a RegExp (options.storyPattern) to the collapsed value - attempting safe auto-fixes via getFixedStoryPath for missing/incorrect suffixes, then reporting invalidStoryFormat with appropriate details. - validateReqAnnotation(...) implements REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION and REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY similarly for @req. - processComment(...) and processCommentLine(...) implement REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT and REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: - They iterate all comment lines, normalize them with normalizeCommentLine, maintain a PendingAnnotation across lines, and collapse multi-line values before validation. - Program visitor in create(context) scans all comments in the file: - const comments = sourceCode.getAllComments() || []; - comments.forEach(comment => processComment(context, comment, options)); This means it works with any annotations present in the file, independent of which rule discovered the associated functions/branches, satisfying the integration intent. - meta.messages defines specific messages and delegates detailed text to buildStoryErrorMessage/buildReqErrorMessage, giving clear and consistent UX: - invalidStoryFormat: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." - invalidReqFormat: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."
2) Shared helpers and format specification - File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts - Defines the canonical format rules (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT): - getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ (relative path, versioned, ending with .story.md). - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ - Provides configurable patterns and examples via nested story/req objects and flat shorthand fields, with JSON schema validation via getRuleSchema(), satisfying quality standards and configurability. - File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts - collapseAnnotationValue(value: string): string - Replaces all whitespace with a single empty string, explicitly documented as handling multi-line values. - Annotated with @story 005.0 and @req REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT / REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT. - getFixedStoryPath(original: string): string | null - Implements safe auto-fix rules for suffix issues (.story, .md, missing extension) while rejecting paths containing ".." (traversal), aligning with the invalid examples in the story. - buildStoryErrorMessage(...) and buildReqErrorMessage(...) - Use the configured or default examples (e.g. "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md", "REQ-EXAMPLE"). - Generate messages like: - "Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md\"." - "Invalid requirement ID \"invalid-format\" for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like \"REQ-EXAMPLE\" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only)." - These messages are what get interpolated into "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}.", providing REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY and good UX. - File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts - normalizeCommentLine(...) explicitly supports JSDoc stars and inline tags, and detects @story/@req/@implements anywhere in the line, directly addressing REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING and robust parsing of comment structures.
3) Tests directly covering story 005.0 requirements - File: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Header: /** * Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Verify valid-annotation-format rule enforces annotation format syntax */ - Describe block: "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" - Valid cases exercise all key requirements: - "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] valid story annotation format (single-line)" with a correctly shaped @story path. - "[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] valid req annotation format (single-line)" with @req REQ-EXAMPLE. - "[REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION] valid block annotations (single-line values)" showing combined @story/@req in a JSDoc block. - "[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT] valid multi-line @story annotation value in block comment" and analogous test for @req. - "[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING] valid JSDoc-style comment with leading stars and spacing" confirming robust parsing. - Invalid cases cover missing and malformed values, path traversal, and invalid extensions: - Missing story/req identifiers both single-line and multi-line. - Invalid @story extension (.story or no extension) with expected auto-fix outputs and detailed messages. - Path traversal: "// @story ../docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md" with appropriate error details. - Invalid @req IDs (e.g. "invalid-format", malformed multi-line IDs) with detailed error messages. - Tests also verify: - Configuration error reporting and safe fallback (invalid regex patterns in options) via messageId: "invalidRuleConfiguration", while still enforcing default patterns (quality standards & robustness). - That configured examples appear correctly in error messages (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY and documentation alignment).
4) Documentation matching the story - File: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md - Top-level description: "Validates that `@story`, `@req`, and `@implements` annotations follow the correct format and syntax rules..." which is exactly the story’s goal. - Explicitly references this story and requirements: @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION @req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION @req REQ-PATH-FORMAT @req REQ-REQ-FORMAT - Contains: - Detailed explanation of default patterns for paths and requirement IDs. - Examples of correct and incorrect annotation formats that match (and extend) the examples in the story. - Explanation of multiline behavior and whitespace collapsing. - Configuration options (nested and flat), schema behavior, and error messaging examples. - This satisfies the story’s "Documentation: Format specification with examples of valid and invalid annotations" acceptance criterion.
5) Test run evidence - The project test run (npm test -- --verbose) includes: - PASS tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Valid and invalid cases for REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, and @implements-related constraints all pass. - Overall Jest summary: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 266 passed, 266 total - This confirms that the implementation of the rule and its edge cases is fully covered and currently passing.
6) Integration and quality standards - The rule is implemented as a standard ESLint rule module with: - meta: type, docs, messages, schema, fixable, matching eslint best practices. - create(context) returning a Program visitor that uses context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(), so it naturally works alongside function (require-story-annotation) and branch (require-branch-annotation) rules over the same codebase. - Plugin configuration tests (tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts and tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts) show the rule is correctly registered and behaves with recommended/strict configs, supporting the "Quality Standards" and "Integration" acceptance criteria.

The accompanying tests explicitly reference this story and its requirements, thoroughly cover valid and invalid scenarios, and are all passing.
